Elena — thanks for the patience. Please find our consolidated responses attached (redwood_peregrine_rfi_answers_v1.pdf) and a simplified network diagram (network-diagram-vpc-onprem.svg). Summary of key points below; full answers in the PDF.

1) Network isolation & egress controls- We support both VPC-hosted private control planes and fully on‑prem air‑gapped installs. For VPC deployments we provide customer‑managed egress policies using an egress gateway you control (iptables/egress-NAT) and support placement in private subnets with no public IPs. For on‑prem/air‑gapped installs we provide an offline installation bundle and a patch-transfer workflow (signed artifacts over controlled transfer). See diagram for suggested NAT/proxy placement.

2) Operator access & keystore model- Operator access is role‑based with mutually authenticated operator sessions. For cryptographic keys we support three models: Redwood KMS (hosted), customer KMS via standard KMS APIs (AWS KMS/Azure Key Vault/GCP KMS), and HSM-backed customer keys (PKCS#11). We do not hold customer private keys when HSM model is requested; Redwood only stores KM references. We provide an operator separation matrix and an audited operator session log shipped to customer telemetry endpoints.

3) Patching, upgrades & air‑gap workflows- For online VPC installs we provide rolling upgrades with canary routing and automatic rollback on health‑check regressions. For air‑gapped/on‑prem we supply signed patch bundles and a documented patch promotion process: staging -> validation lab -> production via signed media transfers. We include SHA256 checksums and SBOM for each release. Expected maintenance window coordination and rollback playbook included in the attachment.

4) Telemetry, audit logs & retention- Customers control telemetry egress endpoints. For private control‑plane installs we push structured telemetry to customer endpoints (S3, syslog, or HTTPS collector). Default telemetry retention within Redwood hosted analytics is 90 days; for private deployments the customer sets retention policies. We provide a retention options table and guidance for PII scrubbing prior to transit.

5) SBOM & provenance- Each release includes SPDX/CSV SBOM, signed release manifest, and a verifiable provenance chain. We can provide per‑release SBOM artifacts for external audit and for inclusion in your supply‑chain review.

Attachments: redwood_peregrine_rfi_answers_v1.pdf (detailed Q&A, policy excerpts, operator matrix), network-diagram-vpc-onprem.svg (simplified topology).

If you'd like to run a live walkthrough of the attachment, we can schedule 30 minutes with our infra and security engineers this week.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Elena,

Answers inline below.

- HSM unsealing/operator actions: Unsealing the HSM is not part of routine operator day‑to‑day. Actions that require HSM unseal are emergency key‑recovery (customer‑initiated), rekey operations, and initial operator bootstrap during a cold install. Routine operator tasks (start/stop services, apply config, rotate service account credentials) do not require HSM unseal. We can provide an itemized action list and an access approval flow (approval chain + required MFA/auth).

- Patch availability SLA for air‑gapped installs: Standard turnaround for producing a signed patch bundle after a GA release is 3 business days (includes SBOM and signed manifest). For security hotfixes we offer an expedited 24–72 hour window depending on severity and signing approval. These timelines assume the customer provides the same approval windows; we detail exceptions in the attached playbook.

I'll add the HSM operator action list and SLA table as a short annex and re-send. Would you prefer it inline in the RFI PDF or as a standalone annex?

Thanks,
Naomi
